title: Runtime release readiness manifest and engineering gates
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Purpose

This page defines the cross-functional release readiness manifest and engineering gates for any major or minor runtime change that touches the serving stack: kernel scheduler, GPU dispatch path, K/V cache, telemetry surface, or client-facing runtime gateway. The goal is a single, repeatable checklist that combines architecture review, kernel scheduling safety, profiling and benchmarking artifacts, release notes, known-issues enumeration, and runbook activation criteria.

Scope

Applies to: runtime-gateway, kernel-scheduler, gpu-dispatcher, kvcache-service, telemetry-collector, runtime-agent.
Excludes: control-plane-only changes (console UI, billing) unless they alter routing or model selection logic.

Quick summary of gates

1) Architecture review complete and signed off.
2) Scheduler kernel tests green on canary hardware profile.
3) Profiling and regression benchmarks executed; no >5% tail-latency regressions without mitigation.
4) Benchmark suite (unit, integration, e2e) completed and artifacts uploaded.
5) Runbooks updated + pager paths validated.
6) Known issues triage completed and mitigations documented.
7) Release notes prepared and release artifact zipped.

Owners & responsibilities

| Area | Primary owner | Secondary owner | Acceptance criteria |
|------|---------------|-----------------|--------------------|
| Architecture & API contract | Sanjay Rao | Hannah Li | ADR recorded; compatibility matrix updated |
| Kernel scheduling changes | Dmitri Ivanov | Lee Chen | Scheduler unit tests + scheduling-safety fuzzing pass |
| Profiling & regression | Aisha Kumar | Priya Natarajan | Profiling report produced; root-cause analysis for any regression |
| Benchmarking & cost | Marcus Perez | Owen Wright | Bench harness artifacts uploaded; cost delta <= budget gate |
| Runbooks & Ops playbooks | Renee O'Connell | SRE oncall | Runbook publishes TTLs and escalation paths |

Pre-release checklist (detailed)

1) Architecture and design
   - Add/update ADR or design note with backward compatibility section.
   - Document expected behavior under degraded resources (eviction semantics, model swap).
   - Confirm model variant routing policies and fallback order.

2) Kernel & scheduler safety
   - Run scheduler unit tests (fast): ./tools/test-scheduler --unit --filter=priority_*
   - Run cooperative preemption simulation: ./tools/sim-scheduler --scenario=preempt-coop --iterations=500
   - Execute safety fuzzing: ./tools/sched-fuzz --duration=4h --seed=stable
   - Validate kernel handoff traces: trace_id = <sample>; verify no missing commit markers.
   - Acceptance: no assertion failures and <0.1% missed deadline events on canary pool.

3) Profiling & microbenchmarks
   - Produce before/after profiling bundle for the change: perf-bundle --baseline=main --candidate=feature/branch --out=perf-bundle.zip
   - Required profiler outputs: occupancy.csv, kernel-latencies.json, kv-cache-hitrates.csv, p99_token_latency.tsv
   - Focus tests: short (<=32 tokens), medium (128 tokens), long (1024 tokens), streaming scenarios.
   - Gate: p99 token latency regression <=5% on canonical workloads; any higher requires mitigation plan.

4) Benchmarking suite (integration + e2e)
   - Run mixed-workload harness: ./bench/run-mixed --profile=prod-sim --duration=30m --concurrency=100
   - Run SLO simulation: ./bench/slo-sim --traffic-profile=canary --seed=42
   - Cost sensitivity: ./bench/cost-delta --quant=quant-8 --baseline=main
   - Upload artifacts to perf-lab artifacts bucket: gs://perf-artifacts/runtime/releases/<release-tag>/
   - Gate: no >10% cost-per-token increase vs baseline without corresponding quality improvement.

5) Observability & telemetry
   - Ensure new metrics registered in telemetry-collector and dashboard panels created: runtime.kernel.commit_latencies_ms, runtime.kvcache.hit_rate, runtime.scheduler.preempt_events_total
   - Validate traces are sampled at p=1% for production-like jobs and p=100% on canaries for 24h.
   - Ensure tracing spans include kernel_id, shard_id, request_class, token_count.

6) Runbooks and operational readiness
   - Update runbook sections: "eviction-reconstruction", "scheduler-deadline-exceedances", "kvcache-warmup".
   - Add step-by-step remediation with commands, expected side-effects, and ownership. Example command: kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deploy/gpu-dispatcher --grace-period=60
   - Pager test: run a simulated incident drill with oncall and confirm escalation chain works.

7) Known issues and mitigations
   - Add any pre-existing known issues that could interact with the change (e.g., NVLINK degradation profile, nvdriver-compatibility-510).
   - Provide mitigation matrix: severity, mitigation steps, rollback hints, communication template.

Sample mitigation table

| Issue | Severity | Immediate mitigation | Runbook link |
|-------|----------|----------------------|--------------|
| NVLINK interconnect degradation on p4d | high | Move non-critical workloads, enable slot isolation | /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/known-issues/nvlink-interconnect-degradation-and-remediation-2026 |
| K/V cache cold-start regression | medium | Increase warmup-provisioning for canary; prefill common prefixes | /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/dynamic-kvcache-resilience-and-warmup-playbook-2026 |

Release artifact and notes template

- Artifact name: runtime-release-<tag>.zip
- Contents: binary images, perf-bundles/, benchmark-results.csv, profiling/ (occupancy/latency), release-notes.md, runbooks/updated_runbooks.pdf

release-notes.md (boilerplate)

Title: <release-tag> — short summary\\nAffected Services: runtime-gateway, kernel-scheduler\\nSLO impact: none expected; if any, see SLO section below.\\nMigration steps: none (runtime-internal) / manual rollout matrix attached.\\nKnown regressions: list here (if any) and mitigation.

SLO gates and metrics (hard)

- p50 token latency: no change >3% (informational)
- p95 token latency: no change >5% (investigate)
- p99 token latency: no change >5% (blocker unless mitigated)
- Error rate (user-visible 5xx): <0.1% increase allowed during canary window
- Scheduler missed-deadlines: <0.05% over 24h on canary pool

Kernel change rollback procedure (fast path)

1) Trigger canary rollback: kubectl -n runtime set image deployment/kernel-scheduler kernel-scheduler=registry.redwood/runtime/kernel-scheduler:<previous-tag>
2) Restart dependent daemons in order: gpu-dispatcher -> kvcache-service -> runtime-gateway (graceful drain between each with 60s).
3) Re-run smoke checks: ./tools/runtime-smoke --endpoints=smoke-list.txt
4) If rollback fails, escalate to platform-release@redwood and open an incident with "runtime-kernel-rollback" template.

Post-release tasks

- Monitor telemetry for 72 hours at increased sampling (p=5%).
- Run cost sampling job to detect any regression in GPU utilization or per-token cost.
- Retain perf artifacts for 180 days.
- Conduct a 2-week retrospective with owners and capture follow-ups.

Checklist sign-off (required fields)

- [ ] Architecture review (owner + date)
- [ ] Kernel safety tests (owner + date)
- [ ] Profiling bundle uploaded (artifact path)
- [ ] Benchmark suite passed (artifact path)
- [ ] Runbooks updated and linked (URLs)
- [ ] Release notes published (link)
- [ ] Release artifact uploaded (path)

References and useful commands

- Profiling: perf-bundle --baseline=main --candidate=feature/x --out=/tmp/bundle.zip
- Mixed workload benchmark: ./bench/run-mixed --profile=prod-sim --duration=30m --concurrency=100 --out=results.csv
- Scheduler fuzz: ./tools/sched-fuzz --duration=4h --out=fuzz-results.json
- Upload artifact: gsutil cp -r perf-bundles/<tag> gs://perf-artifacts/runtime/releases/<tag>/

Appendix: Minimal verification script (example)

# Minimal smoke script (bash excerpt)
# 1) Check health endpoints
# 2) Run 50 short token requests and assert no 500s

set -e
for ep in $(cat smoke-list.txt); do
  status=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' $ep/health)
  if [ "$status" != "200" ]; then
    echo "Health check failed for $ep"; exit 1;
  fi
done

python - <<'PY'
import requests
urls = open('smoke-list.txt').read().splitlines()[:5]
for u in urls:
    r = requests.post(u + '/v1/generate', json={'input': 'hello', 'max_tokens': 8}, timeout=5)
    assert r.status_code == 200
print('smoke ok')
PY

End of document.
